what_it_does: This is a specialized camera chip for long-wavelength infrared imaging—the kind used in thermal cameras and thermal analysis of electronic chips. It improves the signal-to-noise ratio (clarity) and dynamic range (the span from darkest to brightest) by replacing bulky power-hungry analog circuits with a new approach: light-driven current-to-phase conversion. Instead of converting the sensor's electrical current into a voltage or frequency (standard approaches), it converts it into a phase shift of a light signal generated by only the photocurrent itself, requiring no extra power supply. The chip compresses the signal directly at each pixel before transmission, reducing interference over long wires and cutting power consumption. A 20-bit counter at each pixel ensures high resolution.
